Automotive / New vehicle dealerships

From OEM lead to delivered vehicle, with every step visible

Authorized car dealerships juggle OEM targets, many lead sources, demo fleets, allocations, finance, insurance and registration. We connect the OEM DMS, CRM and WhatsApp so every enquiry gets a fast answer, test drives and quotes follow one process, and buyers know where their vehicle stands until handover.

The challenge

What makes new vehicle dealerships different.

01

OEM, website, marketplace and social leads arrive in separate portals, and many OEMs track lead follow-up in their DMS, which consultants update late or not at all.

02

Demo vehicles are double-booked or parked at the wrong branch, so test drives are canceled at the last minute.

03

On-road quotes are built by hand from price lists, state road tax, insurance and accessory packs, and different consultants quote the same buyer differently.

04

Buyers on long waiting periods call repeatedly for allotment and delivery dates, and cancellations rise when they hear nothing.

Where automation helps

Practical uses for new vehicle dealerships.

01

Unified lead queue

OEM portal, website, Meta, Google and marketplace leads in one queue with deduplication, a consented WhatsApp acknowledgement, consultant assignment and first-call timers, with the OEM DMS kept up to date.

02

Demo-fleet aware test drives

Showroom and home test-drive slots by variant and branch, with reminders, a license check at key handover and a follow-up after every drive.

03

Consistent on-road quotes

Quotes built from the approved price list, state registration charges and insurer quotes, with accessories and extended warranty shown as clear opt-ins and discounts above a limit routed to the sales manager.

04

Exchange evaluation inside the deal

An exchange request books an evaluator slot and feeds the manager-approved valuation back into the quote, so the buyer sees one consolidated offer.

05

Booking-to-delivery status

One tracker for allotment, payments, loan disbursal, insurance, registration, HSRP and PDI, with waiting-period updates in wording the sales manager approves.

06

Renewal and warranty follow-through

Insurance renewal and extended-warranty reminders for owners the dealership sold to, sent only with consent and handled by licensed staff.

Automation blueprints

The automations we would start with.

Open each blueprint for its trigger, steps, tools, human checkpoint, data handling, deliverables, and measures.

Discover and enquireStandard3–5 weeks

Instant lead response, qualification and routing

Leads from OEM portals, the website, ad lead forms, marketplaces, missed calls and WhatsApp are deduplicated, acknowledged within minutes where the buyer has opted in, qualified with a short flow and assigned to a consultant with a first-call timer.

New vehicle dealerships · Pre-owned vehicle dealers · EV & two-wheeler dealers

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Dealerships pay for leads from several sources, but each source has its own portal and inbox. Leads that arrive after hours or during busy showroom periods wait, duplicates are called twice by different consultants, and buyers who hear nothing soon enquire at the next dealership.

Trigger

A new lead arrives from an OEM lead portal export or API, a website form, Meta or Google lead forms, a marketplace dealer panel, an IVR missed call or a click-to-WhatsApp chat.

How it runs

  • Normalize the lead, match the mobile number against open DMS or CRM enquiries and merge duplicates, keeping every source for attribution.
  • Check the consent captured on the source form; opted-in buyers receive an approved WhatsApp template, and everyone else becomes a call task.
  • Run a short WhatsApp flow for model, variant or fuel, purchase timeframe, exchange and finance interest, and classify free-text questions without answering price or offer questions.
  • Assign the lead by brand, branch, model and language, create or update the enquiry in the DMS or CRM and start a first-call timer.
  • Alert the team leader in Slack when the timer lapses, and reassign after a second lapse under the rules the sales manager sets.
  • Log source, response times and outcome for the weekly lead review.

Human checkpoint

The sales consultant makes the first call and answers anything about price, discounts, exchange value or finance. Team leaders handle reassignment, and the sales manager approves templates, qualifying questions and routing rules before launch and after every change.

Conversations are kept for the period the dealership's retention policy sets, model calls run under terms that exclude training on the data, and a consultant's access ends the day they leave.

  • Duplicate lead rate
  • Lead-to-test-drive rate

Test drive and evaluationStandard3–4 weeks

Test-drive and test-ride booking against the demo fleet

Buyers pick showroom or home test drives from slots tied to real demo-vehicle availability by variant and branch, get reminders and can reschedule in one tap. Consultants see the day's schedule and get a follow-up prompt after each drive.

New vehicle dealerships · EV & two-wheeler dealers

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Demo vehicles are shared across consultants and branches and booked on a whiteboard or in a group chat. Double bookings, a demo vehicle away for service or a missed reminder lead to canceled drives, and buyers who did drive often get no structured next step.

Trigger

A buyer chooses a test drive in the qualifying flow or on the website, or a consultant requests a slot from the CRM.

How it runs

  • Read demo-fleet availability by variant, fuel type and branch, excluding vehicles marked for service, charging or cleaning.
  • Offer showroom slots, and home slots within the radius the showroom manager sets, then hold the vehicle and consultant on confirmation.
  • Send an approved confirmation with location, documents to bring and a reschedule button, then a reminder before the slot.
  • Prompt the consultant to check the original driving license in person and record start and end odometer readings.
  • After the drive, ask one feedback question and create the consultant's next action, such as a quote or a second drive.

Human checkpoint

The consultant confirms every home test drive, checks the driving license before handing over keys and decides whether the drive goes ahead. The showroom manager sets the home-drive radius, time limits and which variants may leave the showroom.

Quote, finance and bookingAdvanced5–7 weeks

On-road quote with finance and insurance desk handoff

Consultants issue consistent on-road quotes from approved price lists and insurer quotes, with optional items shown as clear opt-ins. Finance and insurance requests move to the F&I desk with the buyer's consent, and lender disclosures and decisions stay with the lender.

New vehicle dealerships · Pre-owned vehicle dealers

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Quotes are typed from price sheets, so one buyer can get different figures from different consultants, optional accessories look mandatory and discount approvals happen on calls. Finance interest is passed to lender executives on chat without consent or tracking, and nobody can see why a booking is waiting on the loan.

Trigger

A consultant marks a quote as requested in the CRM or DMS after a test drive or a pricing enquiry.

How it runs

  • Assemble the quote from the approved price list, the state registration and road tax table, an insurer quote and selected accessories, with an issue date and validity period.
  • Show accessories, extended warranty and add-on covers as separate optional lines the buyer chooses, never preselected.
  • Route discounts or exchange bonuses above the consultant's limit to the sales manager for approval before the quote is sent.
  • Send the quote as a secure link and record its version against the enquiry.
  • On request and with consent, share the minimum details with the buyer's chosen lender through its DSA or sourcing channel, and track status to sanction and disbursal.
  • Hand insurance selection to the licensed insurance executive, and log the policy and add-ons the buyer chooses.

Human checkpoint

The sales manager approves discounts and exchange values above limits. The lender makes every credit decision and issues its Key Facts Statement; the dealership shows EMIs only as indicative. A licensed insurance executive explains cover and add-ons, and the buyer chooses.

Allotment, paperwork and deliveryStandard4–6 weeks

Booking-to-delivery tracker with waiting-period updates

Every booking gets one tracker for allotment, payments, loan disbursal, insurance, registration, accessories and pre-delivery inspection. Buyers get regular status updates in approved wording, and coordinators see what is blocking each delivery.

New vehicle dealerships

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

On popular models buyers wait weeks or months, and status lives in the OEM allocation portal, the DMS, the finance desk and the accessories team. Buyers call for updates, consultants guess dates, and silence or a missed promise often ends in a canceled booking.

Trigger

A booking amount is receipted in the DMS against a model, variant and color.

How it runs

  • Create the delivery record with milestones for allotment, payment, loan disbursal, insurance, registration, accessories, PDI and handover, each with a named owner.
  • Read allocation and in-transit status from OEM portal exports, and update milestones as owners mark them done.
  • Send the buyer a scheduled waiting-period update in approved wording; a delivery date is shared only after the delivery coordinator confirms allotment.
  • Alert the milestone owner and the delivery coordinator when an item stalls beyond the agreed number of days.
  • Offer delivery slots once every milestone is complete, and send a handover checklist with the documents to bring.

Human checkpoint

The delivery coordinator confirms allotment and every delivery date before it reaches the buyer. Any change to a promised date, or a request to switch model or color, goes to the sales manager.

Allotment, paperwork and deliveryStarter2–4 weeks

Registration, HSRP and RC status tracking

After invoicing, each vehicle's registration checklist, Vahan application, tax payment, number plate fitment and RC dispatch are tracked with a named owner. Buyers get status updates, and registration staff see what is missing before the file is submitted.

New vehicle dealerships · EV & two-wheeler dealers

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Registration depends on correct buyer documents, insurance, tax payment and each state's process, followed by HSRP fitment and RC dispatch. Missing documents surface late, temporary registrations run close to expiry, and buyers call the showroom to ask where their plates and RC are.

Trigger

The vehicle invoice is generated in the DMS, or a temporary registration is issued.

How it runs

  • Create the registration checklist for the buyer's state and vehicle category, including identity and address proof, PAN or Form 60, insurance and hypothecation details.
  • Collect missing documents through a secure upload link that asks for masked Aadhaar where it is accepted, and queue them for staff verification.
  • Record the Vahan application number and status that the registration executive enters after submission.
  • Track tax and fee payment, registration number allotment, HSRP fitment appointment and RC dispatch, updating the buyer at each step.
  • Alert the registration lead when a file stalls or a temporary registration nears its end date.

Human checkpoint

The registration executive verifies every document and submits each application on Vahan personally; the automation never submits to a government portal. Name mismatches, other-state addresses and company registrations go to the registration lead.

Feedback, renewals and upgradeStarter3–4 weeks

Consented insurance renewal and extended-warranty reminders

Owners who agreed to renewal messages get reminders before policy and warranty expiry. Insurance renewals go to the licensed insurance executive for customers the dealership may serve under its insurer appointment, and extended warranties are offered only while the vehicle is eligible.

New vehicle dealerships · Service centres & workshops

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Renewal dates sit in insurer portals and DMS fields, so owners hear from aggregators first and lapses go unnoticed. Extended-warranty eligibility windows close before anyone mentions them, and blanket calls to owners who never agreed to them break consent and TRAI preference rules.

Trigger

A daily job finds policies or standard warranties expiring within the windows the dealership sets.

How it runs

  • Read policy and warranty expiry dates from the DMS and the insurer or MISP records.
  • Check consent for renewal messages, the owner's call preferences and whether the owner may be served under the dealership's insurer appointment.
  • Send a reminder with the expiry date and a request-a-quote button; no premium is quoted automatically.
  • Create a task for the licensed insurance executive to prepare quotes in the insurer system and discuss cover with the owner.
  • For extended warranty, check the OEM's eligibility window and kilometer limit, and offer it as an option by message or at the next service visit.

Human checkpoint

The licensed insurance executive explains cover, add-ons and premiums, and the owner chooses. Warranty eligibility and claims are decided under the OEM's terms by the warranty in-charge, not by the automation.

Tools
